title: The Size of a Packet and the Margin of Safety

scenes.tts: What sets the size of one packet? And how far above threshold does a normal response sit?
scenes.visual: One vesicle releasing into the cleft, with the two questions on screen.
scenes.narration: What sets the size of one packet? And how far above threshold does a normal response sit?

scenes.tts: With the muscle membrane and the recording held steady, the size depends on two things. How much transmitter the vesicle holds, and how many receptors face it.
scenes.visual: Two labels: vesicle filling; receptors facing it. Small note: membrane and recording held steady.
scenes.narration: With the muscle membrane and the recording held steady, the size depends on two things. How much transmitter the vesicle holds, and how many receptors face it.

scenes.tts: Acetylcholine crosses the gap and binds nicotinic receptors. A receptor normally needs two acetylcholine molecules bound to open.
scenes.visual: The nicotinic receptor (from the 2BG9 structure); two ACh molecules dock in its two binding pockets and the pore opens.
scenes.narration: Acetylcholine crosses the gap and binds nicotinic receptors. A receptor normally needs two acetylcholine molecules bound to open.

scenes.tts: The channel passes both sodium and potassium. So its reversal potential, where its current changes direction, sits near zero millivolts.
scenes.caption: The channel passes both sodium and potassium. So its reversal potential, where its current changes direction, sits near 0 mV.
scenes.visual: Na⁺ and K⁺ both pass through the open pore. Label: reversal potential ≈ 0 mV.
scenes.narration: The channel passes both sodium and potassium. So its reversal potential, where its current changes direction, sits near 0 mV.

scenes.tts: Now recall the balance point from the action potential lesson.
scenes.visual: The balance-point voltage scale from the action potential films reappears.
scenes.narration: Now recall the balance point from the action potential lesson.

scenes.tts: Treat the fibre as one compartment, with no current injected. Then the voltage moves toward a balance point, an average of reversal potentials, weighted by conductance.
scenes.visual: Card: one-compartment model, no injected current. Vm moves toward the conductance-weighted average of reversal potentials.
scenes.narration: Treat the fibre as one compartment, with no current injected. Then the voltage moves toward a balance point, an average of reversal potentials, weighted by conductance.

scenes.tts: Opening these channels adds a conductance that pulls toward zero millivolts.
scenes.caption: Opening these channels adds a conductance that pulls toward 0 mV.
scenes.visual: On the scale: rest near −90 mV on the left, 0 mV on the right. A new rope from the marker toward 0 mV.
scenes.narration: Opening these channels adds a conductance that pulls toward 0 mV.

scenes.tts: The balance point moves from rest toward zero, and the voltage chases it. The endplate depolarizes.
scenes.visual: A ghost marker (the balance point) slides right; the Vm marker follows a little behind it.
scenes.narration: The balance point moves from rest toward zero, and the voltage chases it. The endplate depolarizes.

scenes.tts: An enzyme, acetylcholinesterase, breaks down acetylcholine and ends each packet's action.
scenes.visual: Acetylcholinesterase in the cleft cuts ACh; the channel closes.
scenes.narration: An enzyme, acetylcholinesterase, breaks down acetylcholine and ends each packet's action.

scenes.tts: One packet nudges the balance point by a fraction of a millivolt.
scenes.visual: One packet: the marker moves a tiny step.
scenes.narration: One packet nudges the balance point by a fraction of a millivolt.

scenes.tts: Each further packet adds the same conductance. But it moves the voltage less than the one before.
scenes.visual: Packets stack as bars; each new bar is a little shorter than the last as the marker nears 0 mV.
scenes.narration: Each further packet adds the same conductance. But it moves the voltage less than the one before.

scenes.tts: Why? As the voltage climbs toward zero, the driving force shrinks. That is the gap between the voltage and zero.
scenes.visual: The gap between the marker and 0 mV shrinks, labelled driving force = Vm − 0 mV.
scenes.narration: Why? As the voltage climbs toward zero, the driving force shrinks. That is the gap between the voltage and zero.

scenes.tts: So each newly opened channel pushes less hard.
scenes.visual: The newest rope pulls more weakly.
scenes.narration: So each newly opened channel pushes less hard.

scenes.tts: The same shrinking push helped stop the spike's peak short of sodium's equilibrium potential.
scenes.visual: A small inset of the spike's peak stopping short of E_Na. Small note: also sodium inactivation and potassium current.
scenes.narration: The same shrinking push helped stop the spike's peak short of sodium's equilibrium potential.

scenes.tts: In this simple model, small responses fall short by almost nothing. Count times size works.
scenes.caption: In this simple model, small responses fall short by almost nothing. Count × size works.
scenes.visual: Label: simple steady-state model, driving force 90 mV, q = 0.40 mV. Table row: 4 packets, count × size 1.6 mV, balance point 1.6 mV (about 2% less).
scenes.narration: In this simple model, small responses fall short by almost nothing. Count × size works.

scenes.tts: For sixty packets, the model comes out about a fifth below simple multiplication. The numbers are on screen.
scenes.visual: Table row: 60 packets, count × size 24 mV, balance point about 19 mV (about a fifth less). Label stays: steady-state illustration, not a measured peak.
scenes.narration: For sixty packets, the model comes out about a fifth below simple multiplication. The numbers are on screen.

scenes.tts: Now the margin of safety. Suppose, as an illustration, the fibre fires at twelve millivolts.
scenes.caption: Now the margin of safety. Suppose, as an illustration, the fibre fires at 12 mV.
scenes.visual: A dashed threshold line at 12 mV above rest across the stacked bars.
scenes.narration: Now the margin of safety. Suppose, as an illustration, the fibre fires at 12 mV.

scenes.tts: The safety factor is the response divided by what the fibre needs to fire.
scenes.visual: Card: safety factor = EPP / depolarization needed to fire.
scenes.narration: The safety factor is the response divided by what the fibre needs to fire.

scenes.tts: Simple multiplication gives a safety factor of two. The balance point gives nearer one point six.
scenes.caption: Simple multiplication gives a safety factor of 2. The balance point gives nearer 1.6.
scenes.visual: On screen: 24 / 12 = 2.0 by count × size; about 19 / 12 ≈ 1.6 by the balance point (steady-state illustration).
scenes.narration: Simple multiplication gives a safety factor of 2. The balance point gives nearer 1.6.

scenes.tts: Smaller, but still comfortably above one. A normal junction fires with margin to spare.
scenes.visual: The gap between the top of the stack and the threshold line highlights, labelled safety margin.
scenes.narration: Smaller, but still comfortably above one. A normal junction fires with margin to spare.

scenes.tts: These round numbers are illustrations. A real junction releases more packets, and needs more to fire.
scenes.visual: Small note on screen: illustrative round numbers.
scenes.narration: These round numbers are illustrations. A real junction releases more packets, and needs more to fire.

scenes.tts: Suppose antibodies remove some of the receptors. Which factor changes: the count or the size?
scenes.visual: Antibodies latch onto some receptors, which disappear. The question on screen.
scenes.narration: Suppose antibodies remove some of the receptors. Which factor changes: the count or the size?

scenes.tts: The size falls. Each packet's acetylcholine finds fewer receptors to open.
scenes.visual: Each packet's bar shrinks. Label: q down.
scenes.narration: The size falls. Each packet's acetylcholine finds fewer receptors to open.

scenes.tts: In this simple picture, the count stays the same. The terminal and calcium set it.
scenes.visual: The number of bars stays the same. Label: m unchanged (assumed).
scenes.narration: In this simple picture, the count stays the same. The terminal and calcium set it.

scenes.tts: So the size depends on vesicle filling and receptors. And big responses fall short of count times size.
scenes.caption: So the size depends on vesicle filling and receptors. And big responses fall short of count × size.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: with membrane and recording held steady, q is set by filling and receptors; big responses fall short of count × size.
scenes.narration: So the size depends on vesicle filling and receptors. And big responses fall short of count × size.
